title: Let an agent debug chip designs in a live Verdi session
summary: A developer built a connector letting an AI agent run Synopsys Verdi, a chip-debugging program, to trace design bugs; he reports testing it on four designs.
agent_role: The agent picks signals, moves the cursor around error times, reads value changes and follows drivers into RTL source. The human gives the debugging question and watches in the GUI; the bridge does not edit or repair RTL.
outcome: The author reports testing with UART TX, AXI-Lite, FIFO and arbiter RTL in licensed VCS/Verdi sessions, on FSDBs up to 2.7 GB.
what_they_did: A developer built a connector that lets an AI agent control a running copy of Synopsys Verdi, a tool for debugging chip designs. It works on the same computer or a remote one. He asked the agent in plain language to investigate bugs, such as why a buffer's "full" signal stayed on. The agent picked signals to watch, jumped back to before the error, studied the signal timelines and found the design code causing it.
how_it_went: The author shares a 1m38s demo where the agent, not a pre-recorded script, chooses each step. He reports it worked on four real chip designs, with recordings up to 2.7 GB, and includes a blind debugging trial.
worth_knowing: It is experimental (version 0.3.3) and needs a paid Verdi license. Connecting to any already-open Verdi window has not yet been tested on its own.
prompt: Using the Verdi Bridge MCP tools connected to my Verdi session for [design name], investigate [describe failure, e.g. why signal X stayed high]. Read the simulation log to find the error time. Add the relevant signals, set the cursor [N] cycles before the error, and inspect their transitions. Trace the drivers of the suspicious signal into the RTL source. Report your findings with times, signal values and file/line references. Do not modify any RTL.

curation.rationale: Unusual domain (chip verification), with a recorded demo of an agent choosing signals and tracing RTL in a live Verdi session. It is still mainly a tool README with limited outcome detail, and the validation is self-reported.
